chunks: All praise be to Allah, Lord of all the worlds
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Rabb al-Alamin' in the opening verse of Surah Al-Fatiha?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted through the lens of *Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah*, emphasizing that all worship and praise are due solely to Allah, the Lord of the worlds (*Rabb al-Alamin*). It sets the theological foundation for the Quran by affirming God's continuous sustenance and lordship over all creation, a concept deeply linked to the Ahl al-Bayt's role as the manifest signs of this divine lordship.
